answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one lab-grown quartz crystal, cultivated over weeks in a licensed mineral lab and registered with a unique lattice fingerprint. A walnut display case holds the specimen, and random audits summon the holder to present that exact crystal in person within a day. One grower cannot tend two crystals at once, and the lab fee in outside money doubles per further crystal on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another crystal, another grower, and twice the prior fee.
